production.note: US model years. Motor Authority (Viknesh Vijayenthiran, 11 December 2024): 'The striking mid-engine supercar will arrive in the U.S. as a 2026 model', 'deliveries set to begin in the second half of 2025'. Aston (am-valhalla-release-2024): 'Production due to start in Q2 2025', 'first deliveries of the limited 999 units to commence in H2 2025'. Still in production; endYear null.

displacementL.note: 3,982 cc (Evo panel: 'V8, 3982cc, twin-turbo, plus three e-motors'). Aston: '4.0-litre twin-turbo V8' (am-valhalla-release-2024).

fuel.note: '1079PS / 1100Nm PHEV powertrain'; 14 km Pure EV range.

drivetrain.note: Three electric motors: 'two driving the front wheels independently and one positioned between the V-8 and' the transmission; Aston: 'torque-vectoring front axle e-motors' (am-valhalla-release-2024). The front axle is electrically driven, so the car is AWD.

transmission.note: 'all-new 8-speed Dual Clutch Transmission' with integrated e-motor.

powerHp.note: Quote (Aston Martin, 11 December 2024): "1079PS / 1100Nm PHEV powertrain combines bespoke 828PS flat plane crank 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 engine with three E-motors delivering a further 251PS". 1,079 PS x 0.98632 = 1,064.2 hp, rounded to 1,064 (combined system output). Motor Authority (motorauthority-valhalla-2026): "The Valhalla produces a combined 1,064 hp"; Evo panel (evo-valhalla-review): "1064bhp (total)".

weightLb.note: Dry weight (weight-order step 4): Aston publishes no curb weight, and Evo (evo-valhalla-review) writes: "Aston Martin quotes the Valhalla's overall dry weight as 1655kg, and does not communicate a with-fluids figure." Quote (Aston Martin): "dry lightweight mass of 1655kg". Motor Authority (motorauthority-valhalla-2026): "Aston Martin lists a dry weight of 3,648 pounds when equipped with lightweight options". 1,655 kg x 2.20462 = 3,648.6 lb, rounded to 3,649 (Motor Authority truncates to 3,648). The figure is for a car with lightweight options; a standard car is somewhat heavier.
